designs.title: Probably Fine
designs.why: Tight, consistent icon system and a dry punchline that reads from across the street; the grid of lit lights does the work. But the lockup is unresolved: PROBABLY FINE is jammed almost onto the last row of labels while a big dead band sits below, and the 16 tiny labels turn to grey noise at tee scale. A couple of glyphs are off-spec (coolant reads like a key, traction-control squiggles tangle).
designs.fix: Rebuild the lockup: open a clear gap above PROBABLY FINE, push it wider and heavier so it anchors the grid, and either enlarge the labels or cut them so the icons speak alone.

designs.title: How to Go to Bed
designs.why: Loose brush line has real hand and warmth, the repetition of 'Turn around.' lands the joke with good timing, and the serif italic captions give it a storybook calm that wears well on either tee. Weak spots: step 3 and 5 anatomy gets muddled, and 6 and 7 are near-identical drawings so the 'Sigh.' payoff is barely shown; the title is small for a header.
designs.fix: Make step 7 its own beat: a visible exhale (puff/breath lines, chest drop, eyes shut tighter) so the punchline is drawn, not just captioned.

designs.title: The Box
designs.why: Clear three-beat gag everyone with a cat recognises, and the tabby rendering in panel 3 is nice. But the construction is broken: the big box spills out of the frame left while its lower body fuses into the panel border, the bed overlaps the right frame line with doubled edges, and panel 1-2 thin lines fight panel 3's heavy weight. The caption is too small and too slight to close the joke on a back print.
designs.fix: Redraw panel 3 so the box and bed sit cleanly inside (or deliberately break out of) one frame with a single consistent line weight, and set BOX NOT SOLD SEPARATELY larger and heavier as the punchline.
